title: Merge World: A very early prototype of a minecraft + hexen inspired game
author: EngineerNo1300
selftext:
Some background on me, I have 15+ years working in the game industry as a video game producer/designer. I have been making games on an AI coding platform I am working on and am mainly just kind of exploring how much of the traditional production process applies. So far it seems like a lot but it has also been pretty humbling.

Some info about the game:

* The game is pretty jank and definitely a prototype but its kind of fun
* The prototype is fully multiplayer, you can play it here: [https://bash.tv/chris/merge-world](https://bash.tv/chris/merge-world)
* For most of the game's development I used Sol or glm 5.3 and for initial planning I used fable
* Ive only been focusing on combat, traversal, and the staff system
* I initially focused on just a test area with movement and the ability to swing a staff. Then added 1 enemy type. Then I added enemies dropping gems. Then the staff system. At a certain point I felt good about those things being the core gameplay and expanded the world and added more enemies
* I went with the voxel style because its light, works on web, and makes iteration much faster than if there were a bunch of heavy assets. I went with pixel art for the weapons because I wanted more detail than what voxels were providing but also wanted something light. Also generating the pixel art variations for all of the staffs is something nanobanana is pretty good at. I plan to work with an artist to replace the art if the game makes it beyond a prototype
* Adding debug commands was super helpful for diagnosing issues with my assets
* I kind of discovered  the rocket jump because I added a spell for terrain destruction and need a way to get out of a hole I created lol
* The staff system is inspired by crafting a lightsaber, where its highly customizable and unique to the person wielding it
* Ive always wanted to make this game but also am having fun integrating suggestions from other people so if you have any ideas for new features let me know!
* Its called Merge World because if you beat the first set of quests your session is supposed to merge with another group that did the same. Each world can only have 4 players but then merges to hold 8. Both groups have to activate the crystal to matchmake. I have not tested this so its probably not working

Some big takeaways:

* Proving out the core gameplay in the smallest most absolute way is still really important. I am not referencing or interfacing with a folder/project structure or using a traditional IDE. Im just speaking directly to an agent in one session so building small and incrementally fits my style. It also keeps me aligned with what the agent is doing
* This kind of relates to how GDDs in traditional development become these bloated docs that no one reads. I think when you start developing with AI and start with a massive set of requirements its kind of the same issue. The artifact will end up being this massive bloated thing that is almost more work to edit than just starting from scratch. I think building small prototypes and connecting/integrating them seems better imho
* Prototyping via a web version seems to be the fastest loop. Easily deployable, shareable, and platform agnostic. I honestly think this is a great replacement for paper prototyping or using a third party engine to prove things out before using a proprietary one
* As nice as web is, its hard to identify a min spec, so I just kind of try to keep things light which has the added benefit of keeping the agent loop really fast
* Prior to this I had almost zero experience with voxel games, so my ability to diagnose or identify better approaches to things isnt great yet but its something I want to dig into
